title: Console: add rollout health verdict + rollback history APIs (authz + pagination)
author: Jada Williams
release_notes: Console backend now exposes rollout health verdict and rollback history endpoints used by the Rollouts UI. Responses are tenant-scoped, RBAC-protected, and support cursor pagination.
body:
Context
Console needs a stable, authz-safe API for: (1) the current SLO evaluator verdict (healthy/unhealthy/unknown) and (2) a timeline of breach/rollback events, with pagination for high-volume routes.
This is part of Auto-rollback on SLO breach integration.

What’s in this PR
- Adds Read APIs:
  - GET /console/v1/rollouts/{rollout_id}/health-verdict
  - GET /console/v1/rollouts/{rollout_id}/rollback-history?limit={n}&cursor={c}
  - GET /console/v1/rollouts/{rollout_id}/policy (for the policy panel; read-only)
- RBAC + tenant isolation:
  - All endpoints require console session + tenant scope.
  - Enforces `rollouts:read` on resource `rollout:{rollout_id}` and validates the rollout belongs to the caller tenant.
  - Soft-fails on missing evaluator data (returns verdict=unknown) rather than leaking internal monitor errors.
- Pagination:
  - Cursor-based pagination for history, ordered by (event_time desc, event_id desc).
  - Default limit=50, max limit=200.
  - Returns `next_cursor` when more results exist.
- Data shaping:
  - Verdict response is normalized for UI consumption and includes a compact `decision_trace_id` for deep links into logs.
  - History response includes only UI-safe fields (no raw query strings, no internal monitor URLs).
- Tests:
  - Unit tests for authz, tenant scoping, cursor correctness, stable ordering.
  - API contract tests for JSON shape.

API details
Health verdict response (summary)
- verdict: healthy | unhealthy | unknown
- reason_code: e.g. latency_slo_breached | error_slo_breached | cooldown_active | insufficient_traffic | monitor_unavailable
- evaluated_window: string (e.g. "5m")
- evaluated_at: RFC3339
- baseline_comparison: "worse_than_baseline" | "not_worse_than_baseline" | "not_applicable"
- decision_trace_id: string
- current_version / candidate_version: string

Rollback history response (summary)
- events: ordered newest->oldest
- Each event has event_id, event_time, type (breach_detected | rollback_triggered | rollback_executed | manual_override | policy_changed), summary fields, and actor (system/user) (no emails)
- next_cursor: string | empty

Notes / follow-ups
- UI wiring will land in a separate PR (Console frontend).
- This PR assumes audit events for rollback executor are emitted elsewhere; this endpoint reads from the same event store but does not introduce new event types.

Risk
Low/medium. Endpoint is read-only but touches authz and tenant scoping. Added explicit tests around cross-tenant access and cursor tampering.

Testing
- go test ./console/... ./rollouts/... (pass)
- console-api contract tests (pass)
- local manual: seeded 10k events and verified pagination + stable ordering

Links
- Linear: ENG-2316
- Related: PR #18455 (evaluator), PR #18488 (audit events)

console/authz: enforce rollouts:read and tenant scoping in rollout routes
rollouts/store: add history query w/ cursor pagination + stable ordering
console/api: sanitize history payload (no raw monitor/query details)
conversation: Chloe Martin (review): Can we confirm the verdict endpoint never 500s due to evaluator store lag? UI will poll this on rollout page load.

Jada Williams (author): Yep — handler maps store timeouts / missing rows to verdict=unknown with reason_code=monitor_unavailable and includes evaluated_at when present. Only 500 on truly unexpected errors (schema mismatch, etc). Added tests for timeout mapping.
Jordan Lee (review): Cursor format: please avoid exposing internal DB ids directly. Also want stable ordering if multiple events share the same timestamp.

Jada Williams (author): Good call. Cursor is now base64 of (event_time_epoch_ms, event_id_ulid) and we order by (event_time desc, event_id desc). event_id is already ULID (public-safe). Added `history_cursor_tamper` test and stable ordering test with identical timestamps.
Benji Okafor (review): Authz: I want to make sure rollout_id can’t be guessed cross-tenant. Do we check tenant_id before returning 404 vs 403? (We generally do 404 to avoid enumeration.)

Jada Williams (author): Implemented: resolve rollout by (tenant_id, rollout_id). If not found, return 404. If found but missing permission, return 403. That prevents enumeration for random ids; still preserves standard permission behavior for known rollouts. Added coverage.
Rafael Mendes (review): From oncall POV, please include a linkable identifier we can paste into logs/dashboards.
Jada Williams (author): Added `decision_trace_id` and `event_id` in responses. Both are also logged with request_id in console-api access logs for correlation.

Naomi Feldman (review): Please confirm history does not return any raw SLO queries or internal monitor URLs. Those are considered internal implementation details and may leak vendor info in Private deployments.

Jada Williams (author): Confirmed. Serializer now only returns reason_code + summary fields. Removed `monitor_query` and `monitor_url` from payload (still available in internal logs). Added contract tests to prevent regressions.
Chloe Martin (approval): Looks good. Thanks for tightening the 404/403 behavior and sanitization. Approving.
